answer: Each agent identity must post a bond that is forfeited when its actions are proven fraudulent, with evidence checked against a public, append-only transaction history. A sybil attacker can create many keys cheaply, but must lock real value behind every one and risks losing it; splitting activity among sable, opal, and onyx identities does not evade the bond requirement. This raises the cost of flooding the economy and makes attacks unprofitable when expected forfeitures exceed any gain.
